title: The ideal PR is 50 lines long
summary: Graphite's PR dataset: changes around fifty lines merge fastest, get the most review per line and are reverted least, while both tiny and huge PRs do worse and the sample skews to trunk-based teams.

assertions.quote: 50-line code changes are reviewed and merged ~40% faster than 250-line changes.
They’re 15% less likely to be reverted than 250-line changes
Sub-10 line PRs are reverted noticeably more than 10-100 line PRs.
There’s a practical limit to how much code your reviewer is willing to read - I suspect that 2k lines is the point
post-5k lines, PRs start getting faster again. I can only assume this is a combination of blind stamps, assumed-safe refactors

verdicts.note: The pattern appears in one dataset and the explanation is the author's guess; rubber-stamping would also hide defects rather than prevent them.

Google changes larger than about 1250 lines get fewer comments on average because they are mostly auto-generated code or large deletions, supporting the stated explanation, but merge time and revert rate for very large changes are not measured.

assertions.quote: We find that Graphite users tend to create smaller PRs in general, since many organizations use a trunk-based development style

verdicts.note: The author flags the confound; no study randomises PR size, so some of the correlation is team maturity.
